Generator and compiler child processes are ended at the deadline; the dsqgen 30 s and 300 s defaults are gone.
A timed-out run exits 124 within the limit plus 30 seconds and leaves a marked partial result that cannot be official, published or submitted, and no reusable partial data.
A decision record, user docs and a changelog fragment are merged with it.

description:
## Problem
No surface lets a user bound a run. dsqgen is stopped by BenchBox after a hard-coded 30 seconds per query (benchbox/core/tpcds/c_tools.py, `DSQGEN_QUERY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`) and 300 seconds per stream set (benchbox/core/tpcds/streams.py), which stops valid work at large scale. dsdgen and dbgen have no limit and no option. The runner cannot stop a run.

## Settled semantics (owner, choice dialog, 2026-11-20)
- Name: "`--timeout SECONDS`, whole seconds only, on `run`, `run-official` and `datagen`"; `timeout_seconds` in the MCP run tool and the Python API; `execution.timeout_seconds` in the config file.
- No default: unset means BenchBox never stops a run on its own.
- Scope: "one clock for the whole invocation, from start to exit: generate, load and execute together. The existing narrower settings (stream, statement) stay as tighter limits inside it."
- At the limit: "BenchBox asks everything to stop (cancels where it can, kills generator processes). If the run has not stopped after a fixed 30-second grace, it writes what it has and exits. So the hard bound is the limit plus 30 seconds."
- After a timeout: "keep a partial result, marked as timed out with the phase and query reached. It can never be official, published, submitted or ranked. Data generated by a stopped generator is not marked complete and is not reused."
- Exit code 124.

## Change
1. A deadline type in `benchbox/utils`, measured with `benchbox.utils.clock.mono_time()`: remaining time, expired check, and a typed error that carries the phase and the query reached.
2. `--timeout SECONDS` on `run`, `run-official` and `datagen`; `timeout_seconds` on the MCP run tool and the Python entry point; `execution.timeout_seconds` in the config file. All resolve to one value in one place (`benchbox/core/run_service.py` is the shared entry today; confirm before editing). Reject zero, negative and non-integer values with a usage error.
3. Every child process BenchBox starts for data or query generation and for compiling the TPC tools gets the remaining time and is ended with its children when it runs out: dsdgen, dbgen, dsqgen, qgen (benchbox/core/tpcds/generator/*.py, tpcds/c_tools.py, tpcds/streams.py, tpch/generator.py, tpch/streams.py, utils/tpc_compilation.py). Reuse one existing process-group kill helper; do not add a fifth.
4. Remove the dsqgen 30 s and 300 s defaults. Reword the error #4409 added so it names the user's limit, not a 30-second one.
5. The lifecycle (`run_benchmark_lifecycle` in benchbox/core/runner/runner.py) checks the deadline between phases and, in the generic query loop, between queries. Never inside a timed section.
6. Backstop: when the deadline passes, request a stop; if the process has not exited 30 seconds later, end child processes, write the partial result and exit.
7. Exit code 124 added to `benchbox/cli/exit_codes.py` with its meaning.
8. Partial result marked as timed out with phase and query reached; refused by `--official`, publish, submit and ranking paths; corpus validation refuses it. A generator stopped midway leaves no manifest that marks the data complete, and a later run regenerates.
9. A timed-out MCP job is failed as not retryable.
10. A decision record under docs/internal or the repository's decisions location (find the existing convention first), user docs for the option, and a changelog fragment.

## Decision gates
No default value anywhere. The 30-second grace is the owner's and is a constant, not a setting. Any other number, message stating a limit, or schema field name for the timed-out marker is shown to the owner before commit if it is visible to users of published bundles; the marker's field name is shown in the pull request body. Windows: where process groups are unavailable, end the direct child and say in the docs what is and is not covered; do not claim more. If marking the partial result needs a bundle schema change, stop and show the owner the field first. Do not change execution-phase defaults here (step 2).

## Verification rubric
Pass, each shown by a test that fails before the change:
- With nothing set, a stubbed generator that outlives 30 s and 300 s is not stopped (single-query and stream paths).
- With the setting, a stubbed dsdgen, dbgen and dsqgen are each stopped at the remaining time; the error names the user's limit, the tool, the phase and, for dsqgen, the query and scale.
- The value reaches the deadline from each surface: `run`, `run-official`, `datagen`, the MCP tool, the Python entry, the config key; the command line wins over the config file.
- 0, a negative number and `1.5` are refused as usage errors.
- A run stopped between phases exits 124 and writes a result marked timed out with the phase reached; that result is refused by the official, publish and submit paths.
- The backstop ends a run whose stubbed phase ignores the stop request, within limit plus 30 s (use a short limit and a patched grace in the test, not real sleeps beyond a few seconds).
- After a generator is stopped midway, the next run does not reuse the data.
- A timed-out MCP job is not retried.
- The strings for a 30-second and a 300-second dsqgen limit are gone.
Also: one real end-to-end check through `make heavy-run`: `benchbox run --platform duckdb --benchmark tpch --scale 1 --timeout 1 --non-interactive` exits 124 with the marked result; the same at `--timeout 600` completes normally. `make pr-preflight` exits 0. The pull request body cites only what was run.

## Guardrails (owner, 2026-11-20)
The agent never posts a stand-in review, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. Arming: `make pr-arm` once; one more attempt only when the refusal named a cause, the agent reported it and the cause is cleared; never a third without asking; `make pr-rerun` at most once and only for a job that never ran or was cancelled by the runner, never for a test that failed. Review threads: reply, and resolve only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise the finding again. Subagents are read-only. Any limit, default, threshold or label text the owner has not already chosen is shown to the owner before it is committed. No file edit by script; use the edit tool. Do not edit a pull request description while its CI is starting; post a comment. A blocked step stops this item; no workaround. No live cloud run. Heavy work only through `make heavy-run`.
